pages.text: Under Titan's Subsurface Seal lies an ocean of salty water, larger than all of Earth's. The $(item)Cryobot$() (research $(thing)Titan's Hidden Ocean$()) melts down into it: stand on the Seal at the bottom of Titan and use it. You come out just under the ice, with the probe's own air for half a minute. An $(item)Oxygen Rebreather$() keeps you breathing after that, and it is as cold as Titan above. Use the Cryobot again to climb back; sinking through the floor brings you up through the ice too.

The ocean is dark water between a $(item)Water-Ice$() ceiling, hung with $(item)Brinicles$(), and a floor of $(item)Abyssal Silicate$(). In the $(thing)Hydrothermal Vents$() mounds of rock rise into glowing chimneys, each crowned by a $(item)Black Smoker$(): water at 400 C pouring out black with sulfides, roaring and bubbling. Its plume lifts and scalds whoever swims into it. $(item)Giant Tube Worms$() ring the mounds, and spread by themselves near a smoker.

Its life, from the bottom of the food chain up: bacteria on the chimneys and in the worms; $(thing)Vent Crabs$() (yeti crabs that farm bacteria on their hairy claws, and brood near a vent) and $(thing)Vent Grazers$() feeding round the vents; $(thing)Brine Jellies$() drifting in open water, stinging what brushes their tentacles; and the $(thing)Ice Eels$() that hunt the grazers.

Its ecosystem is the first for the Ecosphere: $(thing)Vent Grazers$() feed on the chimneys' bacteria and, well fed, multiply; $(thing)Ice Eels$() hunt them, multiply after three meals, and starve after a day without one. So where eels are few the grazers boom, the eels follow, and their feast ends in famine: Lotka-Volterra, with no numbers written in.

Grazers drop $(item)Vent Biofilm$() (cheap Bacterial Cultures in the Fermenter), eels $(item)Eel Photophores$(), jellies $(item)Luminous Mesoglea$() and crabs $(item)Crab Chitin$() (polymer sheet). Together with algae, the $(item)Ecosphere$() builds Stable Ecosystems from them at half the old cost. Abyssal Silicate and water give hydrogen in the Chemical Reactor, as rock does at Earth's vents.
